assignment_order: Consolidated Edison; Craigmiles; Gibson, interleaved with any other same-date cases by alphabetical case name

cases.name: Consolidated Edison Co. of New York, Inc. v. Pataki
cases.form: Form fixed before authorship or balance counts: one signed opinion of the Court after plenary merits submission. Corporate coverage and application of the punishment inquiry are related propositions in one constitutional adjudication with a common full-rationale coalition; they do not justify separate leads or a summary disposition.

fit_alternatives.Stevens: His Ambassador Books opinion supplies the direct identification-versus-punishment distinction and permits precise explanation of this different enacted operation.
fit_alternatives.Souter: His accepted functional inquiry can integrate the fault finding, actual command and legitimate ratepayer argument without a naming shortcut.
fit_alternatives.Stone-Zsela: His approved guarantee-specific coverage and unitary punishment inquiry directly support the full rationale; compare against the strongest eligible lower-count alternative without treating his proposed remedial presumption as adopted.
fit_alternatives.Ginsburg: Her accepted distinction between genuine economic regulation and conclusive punitive adjudication fits the corporate property issue and bounded injunction.

components.component: Affirm injunction against Chapter 190; preserve clerical-correction remand

cases.name: Craigmiles v. Giles
cases.form: Form fixed before authorship or counts: one signed opinion of the Court after plenary merits submission, with distinct dissents by Stevens and Stone-Zsela. The two constitutional challenges receive the same rational-connection answer and produce one injunction disposition. The substantive disagreement over that application requires reasoned dissent but no fragmented lead or component assignment.

fit_alternatives.Thomas: His Beach opinion states the exact conceivable-basis rule and retained Moreno/Cleburne limits now applied to a proved partial curriculum overlap.
fit_alternatives.Souter: His Heller and Romer opinions permit precise reconciliation of actual-disadvantage review with the supported merchandising and accountability ground.
fit_alternatives.O'Connor: Her Beach, Nordlinger and Heller participation commitments support a concise actual-connection ruling while retaining ordinary economic latitude.
fit_alternatives.Kennedy: His Heller family-participation rationale helps explain why availability of less extensive alternatives does not defeat this genuine regulatory connection.

cases.name: Gibson v. County of Washoe
cases.form: Form fixed before authorship or balance counts: one signed opinion of the Court after plenary merits submission. The municipal-liability rule and the limited Rule 56 application form one supported rationale; no separate lead or changed form is needed.

fit_alternatives.Ginsburg: Her Carter opinion directly supplies the source-specific omission, notice and causation framework now applied to supported jail policies.
fit_alternatives.Stevens: His Collins opinion supplies the precise distinction between a constitutional deprivation and its municipal attribution, including the custody-versus-employment distinction.
fit_alternatives.Souter: His Farmer opinion permits careful separation of individual awareness from independent municipal policy without pooling information.
fit_alternatives.Stone-Zsela: His approved application explicitly combines all liability elements with the Rule 56 limits; his conditional future equitable proposal supplies no authorship advantage for the present issue.

components.component: Affirm the limited County return and preserve personal, communications and unappealed dispositions
